subject: Follow-up & smoke-test plan: OpenAI-compat API, SDK swap, and perf checks for Nimbus Health
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Alex Greene <alex.greene@nimbushealth.com>, Priya Desai <priya.desai@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-20T16:12:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up & smoke-test plan: OpenAI-compat API, SDK swap, and perf checks for Nimbus Health

Alex / Priya — thanks again for the conversation today. Quick recap and a pragmatic next-steps plan so your eng team can evaluate migration risk and perf parity without a big lift from your side.

Key takeaways from our call:
- You want an OpenAI-compatible integration so product code changes are minimal (prompt + SDK swap).
- Primary concerns: latency at 512 token sequences, consistency on instruction-following prompts, and a smooth SDK/key rotation path for CI.
- Secondary: on-prem / VPC deployment feasibility for egress/compliance, and how model fallbacks affect cost.

High-level competitive delta (short):
- OpenAI API: market leader in dev ergonomics and broad model availability; drawback = limited routing controls and less transparent unit economics for high-throughput inference.
- Hyperscalers (AWS Bedrock / GCP Vertex): strong enterprise integrations and cloud controls but often higher baseline cost and fewer lightweight batching/caching primitives tuned for LLM serving economics.
- Redwood: focused on production inference economics — predictable reserved capacity, automatic KV/prefix caching, and OpenAI-compatible endpoints so the SDK swap is small while giving you routing and cost controls for large sustained traffic.

Proposed smoke-test plan (what we can deliver this week):
1) OpenAI-compat smoke (goal: SDK swap + functional parity) — run your existing prompts unchanged against our /v1/completions and a Redwood-hosted model. Expected effort: ~30–60m from your eng.
   - We included a short snippet in the attached redwood-openai-compat-snippets.txt and a curl example below.
2) Prompt-diff eval (qualitative) — run a small set (10 prompts) you flagged for instruction-following and compare outputs for hallucination/format stability.
3) Perf quick-bench (quant) — 1000 requests at concurrency 8, sequence length 512, measure p50/p95 latency and tokens/sec. Target: p95 < 450ms for this workload on Dedicated tier.
4) Migration checklist items we recommend you validate: API key rotation, minting scoped test keys for CI, and model pinning semantics.

Quick curl example (smoke):
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/completions 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <TEST_KEY>" 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
  -d '{"model":"rwd-instruct-1","prompt":"Summarize the following patient note: ...","max_tokens":128}'

Node SDK hint:
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.RW_TEST_KEY, basePath: 'https://api.redwood.example.com' });
await client.completions.create({ model: 'rwd-instruct-1', prompt: '...' });

Attachments: small proposal + snippets (two files). The proposal contains cost/throughput ranges for Dedicated vs Hosted for projected monthly tokens.

Ask / proposed next steps:
- Alex/Priya: can you run the smoke curl and share one example prompt that matters most for you? (We can run the perf bench once you give the green light or provide a sample dataset.)
- Marissa/Rachel: will standby to spin up a test key + short Dedicated bench if they want reserved runs.

Happy to sync after you try the curl; if useful I can schedule a 30m working session with your engs tomorrow.

— Sergio
Sergio Alvarez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
sergio.alvarez@redwood.com
(555) 555-0132

Subject: Re: Follow-up & smoke-test plan: OpenAI-compat API, SDK swap, and perf checks for Nimbus Health

Thanks — useful plan. Two quick clarifications before we run anything: 
1) Network/compliance: for the smoke, will test keys route through public hosted endpoints only, or is there a quick VPC path we should use to avoid egress policy issues? Our security team will want a simple answer for the proof-of-concept.
2) Model parity: the prompts we care about are heavily instruction-led and include patient-sensitive formatting — do you recommend any prompt pre-processing or templatization to reduce variability?

If the smoke is truly a drop-in curl, we can run it today. If you need any environment variables or a specific header for region routing, call that out.

Alex
Alex Greene
Lead Product Engineer, Nimbus Health
alex.greene@nimbushealth.com

Alex — quick answers that should unblock the smoke:
- For the initial smoke we will provide a Hosted test key that hits our US-hosted endpoint; no VPC required. If you hit egress constraints we can stand up a short-lived VPC endpoint (requires a bit more setup, ~1–2 business days).
- Prompt stability best practices: we recommend a light templatization step (explicit instruction lines + fixed output schema) and sending examples for the Prompt-diff eval. We can offer a short preprocess shim if you want to keep the client-side code untouched.

Sergio / Rachel: I will create a scoped test key for Nimbus (limited rate) and paste it into the HubSpot deal. Also happy to run the perf bench once Alex shares the prompt set and approves the test window.

Marissa
Sr Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
